steps.instruction: Practice first on scrap of the same thickness as the intended workpiece.
Clean the weld surfaces to bare metal; remove rust, paint, oil, and other material.
Clamp the workpieces securely; bevel thick edges when needed for penetration.
Disconnect vehicle battery power at both the positive connection and ground.
Attach the ground clamp to bare metal near the weld or to the metal bench holding the workpiece.
Practice first on scrap of the same thickness as the intended workpiece.
Clean the weld surfaces to bare metal; remove rust, paint, oil, and other material.
Clamp the workpieces securely; bevel thick edges when needed for penetration.
Disconnect vehicle battery power at both the positive connection and ground.
Attach the ground clamp to bare metal near the weld or to the metal bench holding the workpiece.
With power OFF and unplugged, install the wire spool so it unwinds clockwise.
Secure the spool so it does not spin freely and unravel.
Use the V-groove roller for solid wire or the knurled groove for flux-cored wire.
Flip or replace the roller so the visible size marking matches the wire diameter on the spool.
Fully insert the gun cable connector into the wire-feed mechanism and tighten its knob without overtightening.
Connect the wire-feed control cable inside the machine and tighten its lock ring in the keyed orientation.
Choose shielding gas from the inside-door Settings Chart.
Secure the cylinder upright with two straps, fit the regulator, and wrench-tighten the regulator and gas-hose connections.
Hold tension on the wire, remove bent or burred wire, and guide at least 12 inches into the inlet liner and feed guide.
Seat the wire in the feed-roller groove and latch the idler arm and tensioner.
Set initial feed tension to 3–5 for solid wire or 2–3 for flux-cored wire.
Remove the nozzle and contact tip, then lay the gun cable straight before feeding wire.
Keep hands away from the feed mechanism and do not touch the gun trigger while cold-feeding.
Point the gun away from objects and hold Cold Wire Feed until two inches of wire emerges.
Test drive tension against wood from 2–3 inches away for less than three seconds; increase tension only until the wire bends.
Turn power OFF and unplug, securely latch the door, install the matching contact tip and nozzle, and trim wire to 1/2-inch stickout.
With the Power Switch OFF, plug into a matching grounded, GFCI-protected 120 VAC 20-amp or 240 VAC receptacle with delayed-action protection.
Place the gun on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from grounded objects, then turn power ON.
Press Home, select the requested wire-welding process with the Main Control Knob, and confirm it.
Set wire diameter and material thickness, then verify or adjust wire-feed speed and voltage.
Follow the displayed polarity instructions; do not reuse the opposite process's polarity.
With adequate ventilation and no gas leak, open the cylinder valve fully and set flow to the value on the Settings Chart.
Place the gun on a heat-proof, electrically nonconductive surface and turn the Power Switch OFF.
Let the welder cool, then unplug the power cord.
Remove the ground clamp and disconnect the MIG gun.
Respool by clipping and securely holding the wire, removing the nozzle and tip, releasing the idler arm, and rotating the spool counterclockwise.
Close the gas-cylinder valve, remove the regulator, replace the cap, disconnect the gas hose, and store the cylinder secured.
Secure a 100% argon cylinder upright with two straps, fit the regulator, and wrench-tighten the TIG torch gas hose to the regulator outlet.
Choose tungsten, collet, collet body, and ceramic nozzle sizes from the Settings Chart and match them to each other.
Install tungsten so its tip protrudes 1/8–1/4 inch beyond the ceramic nozzle and lock it with the back cap.
Use a dedicated fine-grit wheel, grind parallel to the electrode length, and use the documented respiratory and eye protection.
Ensure adequate ventilation, open the argon-cylinder valve fully, and set gas flow from the inside-door Settings Chart.
With power OFF, plug into a grounded, GFCI-protected 120 VAC 20-amp or 240 VAC outlet with delayed-action protection.
Place the TIG torch on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from grounded objects, then turn power ON.
Press Home, select TIG, then set rod diameter, material thickness, and output amperage.
Turn the right control ON only when ready to energize the TIG torch; open-circuit voltage is then present.
Close the TIG-torch valve, turn the right control OFF, and place the torch on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface.
Turn the Power Switch OFF, allow cooling, and unplug the power cord.
Remove the ground clamp and disconnect the TIG torch, ground, and foot-pedal cables.
Close and secure the gas cylinder, remove the regulator, replace the cap, disconnect the hose, and store the cylinder secured.
Clean and store the welder and accessories indoors out of children's reach.
Place the bare metal end of the Stick electrode securely inside the electrode-holder jaws.
With power OFF, plug into a grounded, GFCI-protected 120 VAC 20-amp or 240 VAC outlet with delayed-action protection.
Place the electrode holder on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from grounded objects, then turn power ON.
Press Home, select Stick, then set electrode type, electrode diameter, material thickness, and output amperage.
Confirm the displayed polarity and turn the right control ON only when ready to energize the holder; open-circuit voltage is then present.
Set the electrode holder on a nonconductive, nonflammable surface away from grounded objects.
Turn the Power Switch OFF, allow cooling, and unplug the power cord.
Remove the ground clamp and disconnect the electrode-holder and ground cables.
Clean and store the welder and accessories indoors out of children's reach.
